title: METAR & TAF: Read Weather Like a Dispatcher
hook: KDEN 271753Z 33015G25KT... gibberish, or a go/no-go answer?

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds, kid. METARs and TAFs. It's not code — it's just weather with the vowels ripped out to save telegraph money. In eighty years nobody's put them back.
METAR is what IS: station, time in Zulu, wind, visibility, weather, clouds, temp and dew point, altimeter. Same order, every hour, on the hour.

TAF is what WILL be — a twenty-four to thirty hour forecast for five miles around the airport. Watch the change groups: F M means a hard switch. TEMPO means it'll misbehave for a while, then apologize.
For the written, kid: temp slash dew point closing together means fog is filing its flight plan. And B K N or O V C is a ceiling. Scattered is not.
METAR now, TAF later, ceilings are broken or overcast, and converging temp and dew point means get there before the fog does.
A C zero zero dash forty-five H — Aviation Weather Services. All the decoder rings.

quiz.question: Which cloud reports constitute a ceiling?
quiz.explanation: A ceiling is the lowest broken or overcast layer, or vertical visibility into an obscuration. Scattered doesn't count.

quiz.question: In a TAF, "FM1500" means:
choices: A rapid, lasting change to new conditions beginning at 1500Z
quiz.explanation: FM (FROM) groups signal a fast, permanent change to the new conditions at that Zulu time; TEMPO covers temporary fluctuations.

quiz.question: Temperature 12°C, dew point 11°C, sun setting. Expect:
quiz.explanation: A small, closing temp/dew point spread near sunset is the classic fog setup — saturation is one degree of cooling away.
